overview.description: The TechZone Deployer Operator enables automated provisioning of complex IBM software on Red Hat OpenShift clusters. This guide covers creating custom_values JSON structures that content developers add to TechZone environment definitions. When a user provisions an environment, the custom_values JSON is injected at runtime to create a Deployer CR that triggers automated deployments.

key_concepts.concept: Environment Definition - YAML file created by content developers that defines a TechZone environment
custom_values - JSON structure added to environment definition's infrastructure section
Deployer CR - Kubernetes Custom Resource created automatically by TechZone platform using custom_values
Parameters file - YAML configuration in the deployer repository referenced for deployment customization
Post-deployment chaining - Automatic triggering of secondary deployments after primary succeeds

overview.critical_principle: The custom_values JSON structure is NOT Terraform code. It is a runtime configuration that content developers add to the environment definition. When a user provisions the environment in TechZone, the platform injects this JSON to create the Deployer CR. The structure must match the Deployment CRD schema defined in the itz-deployer-operator.

where_it_goes.description: Content developers add the custom_values JSON to the environment definition file in the infrastructure section. This is part of the environment definition YAML that gets uploaded to TechZone when creating or updating an environment offering.
where_it_goes.workflow: 1. Content developer creates environment definition YAML file 2. Adds custom_values JSON to infrastructure section 3. Uploads environment definition to TechZone 4. User provisions environment through TechZone UI 5. TechZone platform injects custom_values at runtime 6. Platform creates Deployer CR in OpenShift cluster 7. Deployer operator executes the deployment

custom_values_structure.description: The custom_values field contains a JSON object with a "deployer" key that defines the deployment configuration. This structure maps directly to the Deployment CR spec.

base_structure.description: Minimal custom_values structure for a deployer-based deployment

complete_structure.description: Complete custom_values structure with all optional fields

field.name: deployer
field.description: Root object containing all deployer configuration

field.name: deployer.repoName
field.validation: Must be a valid repository name accessible to the deployer operator

field.name: deployer.release
field.description: Git tag or branch to deploy from the repository
field.best_practice: Use specific version tags rather than branch names for reproducible deployments

field.name: deployer.parameters
field.description: Path to parameters YAML file relative to repository root
field.note: This file must exist in the repository at the specified release tag

field.name: deployer.ansible
field.description: Ansible execution configuration. When specified, uses Ansible Job mode instead of Tekton Pipeline mode

field.name: deployer.ansible.ansiblePlaybook
field.description: Path to Ansible playbook relative to repository root
field.trigger: When non-empty, switches deployer to Ansible Job mode

field.name: deployer.ansible.requirements
field.description: Path to Ansible requirements file for installing collections/roles

field.name: deployer.postDeployment
field.description: Configuration for automatic post-deployment chaining. When specified, a second deployment is triggered after the primary deployment succeeds

field.name: deployer.postDeployment.release
field.description: Git tag or branch for post-deployment

field.name: deployer.postDeployment.ansible
field.description: Ansible configuration for post-deployment (same structure as primary ansible field)

mode.name: Tekton Pipeline Mode
mode.description: Default execution mode using Tekton Pipelines for complex orchestration
mode.trigger: When ansible.ansiblePlaybook is empty or not specified
mode.behavior: - Operator clones repository at specified release tag - Reads pipeline.yaml and pipelinerun.yaml from repository root - Creates Tekton PipelineRun with parameters file mounted - Monitors PipelineRun status and updates Deployment CR

mode.name: Ansible Job Mode
mode.description: Ansible-based execution using Kubernetes Jobs for configuration management
mode.trigger: When ansible.ansiblePlaybook is specified and non-empty
mode.behavior: - Operator creates Kubernetes Job with two containers - Init container clones Git repository - Main container runs ansible-runner with specified playbook - Parameters file passed as extra vars to Ansible

post_deployment_chaining.description: Post-deployment chaining enables multi-stage provisioning workflows where a secondary deployment is automatically triggered after the primary deployment succeeds. This is useful for separating infrastructure provisioning from application configuration.

use_cases.use_case: Deploy base platform (Tekton), then configure services (Ansible)
Install operators (Tekton), then create operand instances (Tekton)

post_deployment_chaining.behavior: - Primary deployment executes first - Operator monitors primary deployment status - When primary reaches "Succeeded" phase, operator automatically creates child Deployment CR - Child Deployment CR has owner reference set to primary for cascading deletion - Post-deployment executes independently with its own status tracking

environment_definition_integration.description: Content developers add the custom_values JSON to the TechZone environment definition file. This is a YAML file that defines the entire environment offering, including infrastructure configuration, variables, and deployment settings. The custom_values goes in the infrastructure section of this YAML file.

critical_understanding.point: Environment definitions are YAML files created by content developers
custom_values is a JSON object embedded within the YAML infrastructure section
When users provision the environment, TechZone injects this JSON at runtime
The platform automatically creates the Deployer CR using the custom_values
Content developers upload environment definitions to TechZone via the UI or API

environment_definition_integration.complete_environment_definition_example:
# Complete TechZone Environment Definition Example # This is the YAML file that content developers create and upload to TechZone
apiVersion: techzone.ibm.com/v1 kind: EnvironmentDefinition metadata: name: cpd-watsonx-ai title: "Cloud Pak for Data with watsonx.ai" description: "Automated deployment of Cloud Pak for Data with watsonx.ai using TechZone Deployer" version: "5.2.0"
spec: # Platform selection - determines which infrastructure is used platform: "OpenShift Deployer"
# Infrastructure configuration infrastructure: # This is where custom_values goes - embedded JSON in YAML custom_values: deployer: repoName: "deployer-cp4d" release: "watsonx-ai-5.2.0" parameters: "watsonx-ai-5.2.0.yaml" postDeployment: repoName: "deployer-ansible-playbook-example" release: "v1.0" parameters: "variables.yml" ansible: ansiblePlaybook: "playbook.yml" requirements: ""
# Other infrastructure settings cluster_size: "large" storage_class: "ocs-storagecluster-cephfs" worker_nodes: 3
# User-facing variables (optional) variables: - name: "enable_watson_studio" type: "boolean" default: true description: "Enable Watson Studio component"
- name: "enable_watson_ml" type: "boolean" default: true description: "Enable Watson Machine Learning component"
# Documentation and support documentation: getting_started: "https://github.ibm.com/itz-content/deployer-cp4d/blob/main/README.md" troubleshooting: "https://github.ibm.com/itz-content/deployer-cp4d/blob/main/TROUBLESHOOTING.md"
environment_definition_integration.minimal_environment_definition_example:
# Minimal Environment Definition with custom_values # This shows the essential structure content developers need
apiVersion: techzone.ibm.com/v1 kind: EnvironmentDefinition metadata: name: simple-deployer-example title: "Simple Deployer Example"
spec: platform: "OpenShift Deployer"
infrastructure: # The custom_values JSON goes here custom_values: deployer: repoName: "deployer-cp4d" release: "base-5.3.0" parameters: "base-cpd.yaml"

step.title: Create or Edit Environment Definition YAML
step.description: Content developers create a new YAML file or edit an existing environment definition
step.location: Local development environment or TechZone content repository

step.title: Locate Infrastructure Section
step.description: Find the spec.infrastructure section in the YAML file

step.title: Add custom_values JSON
step.description: Insert the custom_values JSON object with deployer configuration
step.format: JSON object embedded in YAML (proper indentation required)

step.title: Validate YAML Syntax
step.description: Ensure YAML is valid and JSON is properly embedded
step.tools: yamllint, yq, or online YAML validators

step.title: Upload to TechZone
step.description: Upload the environment definition to TechZone via UI or API
step.result: Environment becomes available for users to provision

variable_substitution.description: The custom_values structure can reference other environment variables using template syntax, allowing dynamic configuration based on user selections or infrastructure context.
variable_substitution.example:
infrastructure: custom_values: deployer: repoName: "{{ deployer_repo }}" release: "{{ deployer_version }}" parameters: "{{ cluster_size }}-parameters.yaml"
# Variables that can be referenced deployer_repo: "deployer-cp4d" deployer_version: "base-5.3.0" cluster_size: "large"

runtime_behavior.description: What happens when a user provisions an environment with custom_values

sequence.step: User selects environment in TechZone UI and clicks "Reserve"
Platform reads custom_values from environment definition
Platform creates Deployment CR in cluster using custom_values JSON
Deployer operator detects new Deployment CR
Operator clones Git repository at specified release
Operator executes Tekton pipeline or Ansible playbook
If postDeployment configured, secondary deployment triggers automatically
User receives provisioned environment with deployed software

pattern.name: cloud_pak_for_data
pattern.description: Standard Cloud Pak for Data deployment using Tekton
pattern.notes: - Uses Tekton Pipeline mode (no ansible specified) - Parameters file must exist in deployer-cp4d repository at base-5.3.0 tag - Suitable for full Cloud Pak for Data platform deployment

pattern.name: watsonx_with_post_config
pattern.notes: - Primary deployment uses Tekton to install watsonx.ai - Post-deployment uses Ansible for custom configuration - Demonstrates Tekton-to-Ansible chaining pattern

pattern.name: ansible_only
pattern.description: Pure Ansible deployment for configuration management
pattern.notes: - Uses Ansible Job mode exclusively - Suitable for post-deployment configuration tasks - Requires ansible.ansiblePlaybook to be specified

pattern.name: multi_stage_operators
pattern.description: Two-stage operator deployment: install operators, then create instances
pattern.notes: - Both stages use Tekton Pipeline mode - First stage installs operators - Second stage creates operand instances - Demonstrates Tekton-to-Tekton chaining pattern

parameters_file_requirements.description: The parameters file referenced in custom_values must exist in the Git repository at the specified release tag. The file structure depends on whether using Tekton or Ansible mode.

tekton_parameters.format: YAML file with key-value pairs matching pipeline parameter definitions
tekton_parameters.example:
# base-cpd.yaml - Tekton parameters file cluster_name: "my-cluster" storage_class: "ocs-storagecluster-cephfs" namespace: "cp4d" cpd_version: "5.3.0"
components: watson_studio: true watson_ml: true watson_knowledge: false
resources: cpu_limit: "4" memory_limit: "16Gi"
tekton_parameters.location: Must be in repository root or path specified in deployer.parameters

ansible_parameters.format: YAML file with Ansible extra vars structure
ansible_parameters.example:
# variables.yml - Ansible parameters file cluster_name: "my-cluster" target_namespace: "cp4d"
services: - name: "watson-studio" enabled: true - name: "watson-ml" enabled: true
configuration: storage_class: "ocs-storagecluster-cephfs" cpu_limit: "4" memory_limit: "16Gi"
ansible_parameters.location: Must be in repository root or path specified in deployer.parameters

best_practices.practice: Use descriptive parameter file names that indicate version or configuration
Keep parameters files in repository root for simplicity
Document required vs optional parameters in repository README
Use consistent naming conventions across parameters files
Version parameters files alongside code releases

rule.name: Repository Accessibility
rule.description: The repoName must reference a repository accessible to the deployer operator

rule.name: Release Tag Existence
rule.description: The release tag or branch must exist in the repository
rule.validation: Git tag or branch must be valid and accessible

rule.name: Parameters File Existence
rule.description: If parameters is specified, the file must exist in the repository
rule.validation: File must exist at specified path in repository at release tag

rule.name: Ansible Playbook Path
rule.description: If ansible.ansiblePlaybook is specified, the playbook must exist
rule.validation: Playbook file must exist in repository at specified path

rule.name: Post-Deployment Completeness
rule.description: If postDeployment is specified, repoName and release are required
rule.validation: Both repoName and release must be provided in postDeployment object

rule.name: JSON Structure Validity
rule.description: The custom_values must be valid JSON
rule.validation: Must parse as valid JSON with proper syntax

rule.name: Empty String Handling
rule.description: Empty strings in ansible fields indicate Tekton mode
rule.validation: Use empty strings ("") not null for unused ansible fields

issue.name: deployment_not_created
issue.symptoms: Deployment CR is not created after environment provisioning

causes.cause: custom_values JSON is malformed or invalid
Deployer operator is not running in the cluster

remediation.step: Validate JSON syntax using a JSON validator
Check operator pod status: oc get pods -n itz-deployer-operator-system
Review operator logs for errors
Verify custom_values structure matches schema

issue.name: repository_not_found
issue.symptoms: Deployment fails with "repository not found" error

causes.cause: Repository name is incorrect or misspelled
Git credentials are missing or invalid

remediation.step: Verify repository exists: https://github.ibm.com/itz-content/[repoName]
Check repository name spelling in custom_values
Verify operator has access to GitHub credentials
Check IBM Secrets Manager configuration

issue.name: release_tag_not_found
issue.symptoms: Deployment fails with "release tag not found" error

causes.cause: Release tag or branch does not exist in repository

remediation.step: List available tags: git ls-remote --tags https://github.ibm.com/itz-content/[repoName]
Verify tag name matches exactly (case-sensitive)
Use git tag or git branch to confirm existence
Check repository release page on GitHub

issue.name: parameters_file_not_found
issue.symptoms: Deployment fails with "parameters file not found" error

causes.cause: File does not exist at specified release tag
Path is absolute instead of relative

remediation.step: Clone repository at release tag and verify file exists
Check file path is relative to repository root
Verify file exists in repository at the specified tag
Review repository structure and adjust path

issue.name: ansible_playbook_not_found
issue.symptoms: Ansible Job fails with "playbook not found" error

causes.cause: Playbook does not exist in repository
Path is absolute instead of relative

remediation.step: Verify playbook exists in repository at release tag
Check playbook path is relative to repository root
Review ansible.ansiblePlaybook value in custom_values
Test playbook locally: ansible-playbook [playbook.yml]

issue.name: post_deployment_not_triggered
issue.symptoms: Primary deployment succeeds but post-deployment does not start

causes.cause: Primary deployment did not reach "Succeeded" phase
Operator failed to create child Deployment CR

remediation.step: Verify primary deployment status: oc get deployment [name] -o yaml
Check status.phase is "Succeeded"
Review operator logs for post-deployment creation errors
Verify postDeployment has required fields (repoName, release)

practice.rule: Always use the "deployer" root key in custom_values
Provide explicit release tags rather than branch names for reproducibility
Use descriptive parameters file names that indicate version or purpose
Keep parameters files in repository root for simplicity
Use Tekton mode for complex multi-stage deployments
Use Ansible mode for configuration management and post-deployment tasks
Leave ansible fields empty ("") when using Tekton mode
Specify ansible.ansiblePlaybook to switch to Ansible mode
Use post-deployment chaining for multi-stage workflows
Separate infrastructure provisioning from application configuration
Consider Tekton-to-Ansible pattern for platform-then-config workflows
Ensure post-deployment repository and release are valid
Document required parameters in repository README
Use consistent parameter naming across files
Version parameters files alongside code releases
Validate parameters file structure before committing
Test custom_values structure in development environment first
Verify repository and release tag accessibility
Confirm parameters file exists at specified path
Test post-deployment chaining separately

Identify if Tekton or Ansible mode is appropriate
Determine if post-deployment chaining is needed
Find the appropriate deployer repository under github.ibm.com/itz-content
Identify the correct release tag for the desired version
Review repository README for parameters file requirements
Locate the parameters file in the repository
Verify file exists at the release tag
Review parameters structure and required values
Start with base structure: {"deployer": {...}}
Add repoName, release, and parameters fields
Add ansible configuration if using Ansible mode
Add postDeployment configuration if chaining is needed
Validate JSON syntax
Verify all required fields are present
Confirm repository and release tag exist
Verify parameters file exists at specified path
Add custom_values to infrastructure_variables section
Test in development environment
Document any special configuration requirements
